text.text: The blade is an omnipotent tool: its mining level comes from its materials, so it can mine anything that does not demand a higher level, at the blade's own mining speed; on blocks it cannot touch it behaves like a random lump of iron.

On an assembled blade, mining speed is the sum of the blades' and saya's mining speed scaled by the handle modifier, and the mining level is the best of the parts - want a good miner, pick a high-level blade material.

The tooltip has three layers, just like Tinkers' own: by default it shows durability, slash art and trait; hold Shift for the stat numbers (durability / melee damage / attack speed / mining level / mining speed); hold Ctrl for the per-part details.

In the Ctrl view, blades and saya list durability, mining level, mining speed and melee damage, while handles list the four percentage modifiers (durability / attack / speed / mining) - one to one with Tinkers 3's detail view. Only assembled blades keep part records, so a blade forged straight at the forge has no such detail layer.
